cells.tense: The planting is behind you now, and the good result is here.
cells.act: engage the hard part on purpose and see what holds
cells.ask: Sit with the part of this you keep working around — one unhurried stretch, nothing to prepare — and stay until you see what still holds.
cells.core:
You put the effort in on purpose, stayed with it through the stretches that showed nothing, and the good result is here. Taking pleasure in it is part of the work, not a detour from it. This is yours the way luck is not, and it stays yours whether or not anyone else notices it arrived.

One piece is still strange to you. There is a part you have been working around rather than meeting, and circling it keeps it strange. Give it one unhurried stretch, nothing to prepare, no fixing to do. You are not checking whether the effort paid off. You are letting the hard part show what it actually is, the way the easier parts already have.

The next thing worth this kind of care will find you once you stop hunting for it.

cells.tense: A crop not yet ripe is being counted in your head already.
cells.act: join someone in the work so the two streams run as one
cells.ask: Hand one piece of this to another person — a real piece, theirs to pace and shape — and work alongside them rather than over them.
cells.core:
The growth is real, and you are two seasons ahead in your head — next yield, next year, the version where it all holds. From there the garden stops being a place you stand in and turns into something to supervise, and you start watching for the spot where it goes wrong.

The growing has not stopped. Your grip has. There is a difference between caring for something you raised and holding it so hard it can only be defended.

So hand one piece of this to someone else — a real piece, theirs to pace and shape — and work beside them rather than over them. Loosen the grip on that one part. The rest keeps growing while you are not watching, which is how it grew in the first place.
cells.sheetLine: You are guarding the garden instead of standing in it.

cells.tense: You gave the effort and walked past your own share of it.
cells.act: choose which star to steer by and steer
cells.ask: Pick which direction you want a year out, and take the step toward it you keep putting off. Then spend the freed hour on nothing useful.
cells.core:
Wanting your own part started to feel like taking too much, so you gave the effort and left the return where it sat. When something is handed to you now, it goes past. You are practiced at giving and out of practice at receiving, and on this side only one direction of exchange is running.

What is out of true can be set back level. The share you walked past is still where it was, and the side that needs feeding is your own.

Pick which direction you want a year from now, then take the first step toward it you keep putting off. It needs no plan wrapped around it, only the start. Then spend the hour that frees on nothing useful, so something comes back to you from your own effort in a shape you can feel.

cells.tense: Two things sit uneven and something levels them, and you call it the room.
cells.act: drop the wrong approach and keep the commitment
cells.ask: When you catch yourself steadying something, know for a breath that you chose it, then keep the choice you actually want.
cells.core:
In a room where two things sit uneven, something moves to level them, and the something is a person. That person is you. Ask, and you would say the people there just work well together, that you happened to be standing nearby.

You did not happen to be nearby. Setting the level was a move you could have made or left alone, and either way it was a move.

The next time you catch yourself doing it — covering a gap, yielding your turn — know for a breath that you are picking it, then move from the pick rather than from habit. That breath is the whole difference between someone standing in a room and someone adjusting it. Both hands are yours.

attempts.check: The draft says the harvest is 'shared' — the record gives no other people, so nothing may claim anyone else is fed by it; that claim is fixed to the person's own share. A reader could reasonably say they never tended anything and the abundance belongs to someone else's garden, and the Too Little cells are written so that objection still leaves them something to use. The ask survives being wrong: it is one visible act with no promise attached. The sentence that served me more than them was 'the fairness is what makes it fast' — cut. Also cut every 'exactly' and every 'someone, somewhere' hedge.

The line 'you are allowed to enjoy it' served the writer more than the reader — cut, because permission is not mine to grant.
